subject: Literacy
title: My name and its first letter
subtopics: The first letter of my name
objectives: Children will recognise their name card and the first letter of their name.
Children will make marks to show their name with support.
content: Recognising their name card and the first letter of their name, and making marks to show their name with support.
teachingActivities: Always write names with a capital first letter and lower-case letters; use the child’s photo; point to the first letter and say its name and sound only for the four taught sounds; never ask a toddler to write their whole name; accept any mark as name-writing.
learnerActivities: Recognise their name card and the first letter of their name and make marks to show their name with support.
resources: Name labels for pegs and trays
assessment: Observe whether each child finds their name among several cards and points to the first letter with support.
expectedOutcomes: Finds their name among several cards.
Points to the first letter of their name with support.
crossCurricular: Personal, Social and Emotional Development: identity

lessons.title: Find my name
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will find their name card among several cards.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find their name card, hear four sounds and make lines and circles.
lessons.starter: Hold up a name card and say "Whose name is this?" Let the children guess.
teacherActivities: Show each name card and say the name. Point to the photo and the word.
Put five name cards on the floor and ask a child to find their own.
Take the photo away and ask again.
Let each child hold their card and say their name.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the name.
Child finds their card by the word or first letter.
Child holds up the card and says the name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each name card and say the name. Point to the photo and the word. Children: Children look and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Put five name cards on the floor and ask a child to find their own. Children: Child finds their card.
Step 3. Teacher: Take the photo away and ask again. Children: Child finds their card by the word or first letter.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold their card and say their name. Children: Child holds up the card and says the name.

practical.title: Name hunt
steps: Put five name cards on the floor.
Each child finds their own card.
Hold it up and say the name.
practical.safety: Keep the cards smooth and large. Return cards to the basket at the end.

differentiation.support: Keep the photo and use only three cards.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend’s name card without a photo.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Finds a friend’s name card with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards in the basket and say each name.
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child their name written clearly and let them find it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find their name card among several cards" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The first letter
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: The first letter of my name
objectives: Children will point to the first letter of their name.
successCriteria: Points to the first letter of their name with support
Says that it is the start of their name
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find their name card, hear four sounds and make lines and circles.
lessons.starter: Say "Look at the start of my name" and point to the first letter on your name card.
teacherActivities: Show a name card and put a counter under the first letter. Say "This is where the name starts."
Give each child their card and put a counter under the first letter.
For the taught sounds s, a, t and p say the sound if it matches.
learnerActivities: Children look at the first letter.
Child points to the first letter.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a name card and put a counter under the first letter. Say "This is where the name starts." Children: Children look at the first letter.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child their card and put a counter under the first letter. Children: Child touches the first letter.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Where does your name start?" Children: Child points to the first letter.
Step 4. Teacher: For the taught sounds s, a, t and p say the sound if it matches. Children: Child says the sound.

practical.title: Where it starts
steps: Give each child their name card.
Find the first letter with a pointer.
Put a counter under the first letter.
practical.safety: Use large counters that cannot be swallowed. Supervise counters and put them away after.

differentiation.support: Put a counter under the letter and point together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend whose name starts with the same letter.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where does your name start?
questions.expected: Child points to the first letter.

expectedOutcomes: Points to the first letter of their name
Knows it is where the name starts
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say each name.
lessons.homeConnection: Point to the first letter of your child’s name when you write it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to the first letter of their name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Names on my things
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will find their name on their peg, tray and belongings.
successCriteria: Finds their name on a peg or tray
Says that it belongs to them
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find their name card, hear four sounds and make lines and circles.
resources: Name labels on pegs and trays
A bag and a water bottle with names
lessons.starter: Hold up a bag with a name label and say "Whose bag is this? It has a name on it."
teacherActivities: Show a peg with a name label and say "This is Tola’s peg."
Ask each child to find their peg or tray.
Put names on cups and bags and ask "Whose is this?"
Let each child put their bag on their peg.
learnerActivities: Child puts their bag on their peg.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a peg with a name label and say "This is Tola’s peg." Children: Children look at the label.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask each child to find their peg or tray. Children: Child finds their peg.
Step 3. Teacher: Put names on cups and bags and ask "Whose is this?" Children: Child says "mine" or the name.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child put their bag on their peg. Children: Child puts their bag on their peg.

practical.title: My peg
steps: Find your name on a peg.
Put your bag on your peg.
Find your name on your tray.
practical.safety: Make sure pegs are at child height and clear of sharp edges. Supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child to the peg and point to the name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend’s peg and say whose it is.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put all bags back on pegs and say each name.
lessons.homeConnection: Label your child’s things at home with their name.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find their name on their peg, tray and belongings" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Marks for my name
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: The first letter of my name
objectives: Children will make marks to show their name with support.
successCriteria: Makes marks on paper to show their name
Shows their marks to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find their name card, hear four sounds and make lines and circles.
lessons.starter: Say "We can make marks to show our names." Make a mark and say "This is my name."
teacherActivities: Show a name card and say "I can make marks like my name."
Give each child paper and a crayon and say "Make marks for your name."
Write the child’s name neatly beside their marks and say it.
Let the children show their marks to a friend.
learnerActivities: Child watches and says their name.
Child shows and says the name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a name card and say "I can make marks like my name." Children: Children look at the card.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child paper and a crayon and say "Make marks for your name." Children: Child makes marks on paper.
Step 3. Teacher: Write the child’s name neatly beside their marks and say it. Children: Child watches and says their name.
Step 4. Teacher: Let the children show their marks to a friend. Children: Child shows and says the name.

practical.title: Name marks
steps: Give each child paper and a crayon.
The teacher writes the name beside it.
practical.safety: Accept any mark as a name and do not correct. Keep crayons out of mouths and supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Hold the crayon together and make marks.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find the first letter on their name card and copy it with a finger.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes marks to show their name
Shows their marks to a friend
lessons.conclusion: Display the name marks on the wall and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child make marks to show their name on a card or a drawing.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make marks to show their name with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 name check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child finds and talks about their name.
successCriteria: Finds their name among several cards
Points to the first letter with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find their name card, hear four sounds and make lines and circles.
lessons.starter: Say "Where is your name?" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: name cards, pegs and name marks.
At each station ask the child to find their name.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: name cards, pegs and name marks. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask the child to find their name. Children: Child finds their name.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Name stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large cards and soft crayons.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and keep the photo.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to find a friend’s name.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: finds their name among cards; points to the first letter; makes marks for their name.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
Finds their name among several cards
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say each child’s name.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child find their name at home on labels.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child finds and talks about their name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
